title: Add Linear task via uploaded audio
hard_category_focus: Linear task management in signed-in Chrome
breadth_reason: This script extends breadth by testing the full audio upload ASR pipeline against a real CRM surface (Linear) with a decline path when the user's signed-in workspace is not provable.

v7_target.surface_rule: Anticipy must act on the user's actual signed-in Chrome profile with an active Linear workspace; no cloned or hidden browser profiles allowed.
v7_target.proof_rule: Every action, ask, or decline must be accompanied by a fresh, surface-readable proof (e.g., visible Linear record or signed-in workspace indicator) produced by the public build.

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio ASR coverage is the primary proof path for this script, ensuring the engine processes a real audio file rather than relying on pasted text or live microphone input.

real_user_surfaces.name: Linear web app
real_user_surfaces.surface: Chrome browser tab with Linear workspace signed in
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Visible Linear issue creation dialog or task list showing the user's signed-in workspace

real_user_surfaces.name: Chrome profile
real_user_surfaces.surface: User's default Chrome profile with Linear cookies
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Proof that the Chrome profile is the user's own (not cloned) and that Linear is signed in

moments.description: User navigates to https://www.anticipy.ai/app, completes onboarding, and downloads the public installer.
Driver confirms that the user has a real Chrome profile with Linear signed in and that the engine is installed on the user's computer.

moments.spoken_reference_text: Please add a task in Linear for the Brentwood deal to review the contract redlines by Wednesday and tag it priority. If you cannot prove the visible Linear record or my signed-in workspace, decline without writing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: The stranger must generate a fresh audio artifact (e.g., via say command) for each run, ensuring the audio is uploaded through /api/listen/upload and processed by the ASR engine.

moments.description: Engine verifies that the ASR output matches the spoken reference text and that the audio was uploaded from the user's device (not a pre-recorded fixture).

acceptable_outcomes: act: Create the Linear task with the specified details and provide proof (visible Linear record).
ask: Request additional clarification if the intent is ambiguous (e.g., which project to add the task to).
decline: Decline if the visible Linear surface is not signed in or the workspace cannot be proven, without writing anything.

moments.description: Driver observes that the script only uses uploaded audio as primary input, highlighting the gap for transcript paste and live mic modes which are not tested here.

success_criteria: The engine successfully processes the uploaded audio file and extracts the intent to add a Linear task.

If the user's Linear workspace is signed in and provable, the engine creates the task with the specified details (Brentwood deal, review contract redlines by Wednesday, priority tag) and provides a visible proof.
If the Linear workspace is not signed in or not provable, the engine declines without writing any data to Linear.
The entire flow uses the public product path (anticipy.ai/app -> download -> install -> run) and no developer-only shortcuts.
The proof of action or decline is fresh and tied to the public build, not a stale screenshot or log.
failure_triggers: The engine attempts to use a cloned Chrome profile or hidden browser to prove the Linear surface.
The engine writes a task to Linear without providing a visible proof of the signed-in workspace.
The engine accepts a transcript paste or live mic input as primary instead of requiring uploaded audio.
The engine declines without a valid reason (e.g., fails to check the Linear surface at all).
The engine uses a pre-recorded audio fixture or stale ASR output instead of processing a fresh upload.
